title: Add signing step to release pipeline for offline bundles (KMS-backed, publish detached signatures)
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: On-prem offline artifact signing (Private Deployment Automation)
description:
Goal
Add a cryptographic signing stage to Redwood release CI/CD for the v1 air-gapped/offline bundle path. This stage must run in CI (no manual steps), use KMS/HSM-backed keys, and publish detached signatures + provenance metadata alongside the offline bundle artifacts so the on-prem installer can verify fully offline.

Context
Offline bundles will be transferred via removable media / offline repos. Customers need an auditable, repeatable integrity story.
- Bundle build output and manifest generation is tracked in: ENG-3912
- Installer verification work is tracked in: ENG-3914
- Key creation / access policy is tracked in: INT-662

Scope
1) Pipeline stage placement
- Trigger: Release pipeline (tagged release + nightly staging) after bundle assembly completes and bundle manifest is finalized.
- Input: bundle tarball (or directory), bundle manifest, list of included artifact digests.
- Output:
  - Detached signature for the bundle (e.g., <bundle>.sig)
  - Signing metadata (key id / certificate chain if applicable, signing time, algorithm)
  - Provenance references (build id, git SHA, CI run url) written into release metadata and included in artifact index

2) Key access + security constraints
- Signing key must be held in KMS/HSM-backed service (no raw private key material in CI).
- CI runners must assume a narrowly scoped role with permission to call the signer for specific operations only (sign blob / sign digest) and only in release contexts.
- Support separation between staging and production keys (at minimum different key ids; ideally different accounts/projects).
- Ensure log output does not leak sensitive data (no raw bundle contents, no env dumps, no tokens).

3) Publishing + artifact storage layout
- Publish the signature as a first-class artifact next to the bundle in the artifact store.
- Publish a small machine-readable “signature index” file (or attach metadata to the release record) so the installer/docs can deterministically locate:
  - bundle file
  - signature file
  - public key/cert chain (or pinned root) required for offline verification
- Establish naming/versioning convention (must not change without an explicit version bump).

4) Attestation/provenance metadata
- Record and publish:
  - release version / bundle version
  - git commit SHA(s) for bundle tooling + charts/installer (where applicable)
  - CI build id + URL
  - signer key id + environment (staging/prod)
- Note: the actual provenance generation is tracked separately (ENG-3916), but this issue must ensure the signing stage exports the identifiers and publishes/attaches them where the manifest generator can reference them.

Out of scope
- Customer-managed signing keys (v1 non-goal)
- Online verification (must work offline)

Implementation notes / decisions (working)
- Signing model: detached signature over a deterministic bundle digest (NOT over an unstable directory listing). The bundle format work (ENG-3912) should define the canonical bytes to sign (e.g., tarball bytes or canonical manifest digest). This pipeline stage should consume that canonical input.
- Fail closed: if signing fails or signature upload fails, the release should fail and not publish unsigned bundles.
- Replay/downgrade: include bundle version + build identifiers in the signed envelope or signed payload as defined by the v1 spec (see Confluence spec / ADR).

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Release pipeline has a discrete “Sign offline bundle” step gated to release builds (and staging builds in staging env).
- [ ] Step calls KMS/HSM-backed signer (no private key in CI), uses least-privilege role.
- [ ] Produces detached signature artifact and uploads it adjacent to the bundle with deterministic naming.
- [ ] Produces signing metadata (key id, alg, signing timestamp, CI build id) and makes it available to manifest/provenance generation.
- [ ] If signing or upload fails, pipeline fails and does not publish the bundle.
- [ ] Security review sign-off from Marcus Lin (Security Eng) on IAM policy + log redaction.

Links
- Confluence: Release pipeline signing stage design: sources/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/release-pipeline-signing-stage.json
- ADR: Offline bundle signing and verification: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-offline-bundle-signing-and-verification.json
- Threat model: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/threat-model-offline-artifact-signing.json
- GitHub PR (pipeline stage): sources/github/redwood/pr_22163.json
- Slack thread (release coordination): sources/slack/eng-releases/1709041123.json

Test plan
- Staging: run pipeline on a staging release tag to produce signed bundle + signature artifact; verify installer can validate signature offline using staging public key.
- Negative tests:
  - simulate signer outage/permission error -> pipeline fails
  - simulate upload failure -> pipeline fails
  - ensure logs do not contain bundle contents or auth material

Open questions
- Exact canonical signing payload: tarball bytes vs manifest digest (blocked on ENG-3912 final spec).
- Public key distribution: embed pinned root in installer vs ship key/cert in bundle metadata package (needs alignment with ENG-3914).
- Multi-key support/rotation metadata: what key ids need to remain trusted concurrently for N releases (ties into ENG-3919).
comments: 2025-02-06 — Connor O'Brien: Marking P0 given pilot customers are explicitly asking for this (air-gapped integrity). Sahana can you take pipeline wiring; I’ll coordinate with Hanae on key access (INT-662).

2025-02-07 — Sahana Iyer: Started implementation in redwood release pipeline config. Plan is to add a dedicated step that takes the bundle digest file produced by the bundle builder and signs that. Need confirmation from ENG-3912 on canonical bytes/digest to avoid nondeterminism.

2025-02-10 — Hanae Suzuki: INT-662 in progress. Proposed: separate staging/prod KMS keys, CI assumes role with kms:Sign only for those key ARNs. No decrypt, no admin. Will share draft policy for review.

2025-02-11 — Marcus Lin: Security review notes: (1) ensure step only runs on protected branches/tags; (2) ensure CI env doesn’t print token env vars; (3) signature artifact must be immutable once published (write-once path or object lock) to reduce tampering risk; (4) record key id + build id in signed envelope if possible.

2025-02-13 — Sahana Iyer: PR up for pipeline stage and artifact upload. Added guardrails: only runs on release tags and requires "release" context. Upload path includes release version + bundle version. PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_22163.json

2025-02-14 — Connor O'Brien: Reviewed PR. Asked for: explicit failure if signature upload fails; add a small JSON metadata artifact with signer_key_id, ci_build_id, git_sha, signed_digest_sha256 to make installer/docs troubleshooting easier.
2025-02-17 — Sahana Iyer: Updated PR with metadata artifact and stricter error handling. Added log redaction around env debug. Waiting on Marcus for final IAM approval once INT-662 lands.
